quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: The most common type of crash for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania is:

options.text: Single vehicle crash or leaving the road.
Being hit on the side on an interstate.
Driving backward on a side street.
Driving on the shoulder of a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single vehicle crash or leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Single-vehicle crashes where the car leaves the road are the most common crash type for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania. From 2009 to 2011, there were 2,293 of these crashes and 45 deaths.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic from both directions cannot cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. Worry, anger, fear, or sadness make it hard to concentrate on driving. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm and in control.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane of space.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane of space.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has the same rights as any other vehicle and needs a full lane. Even if there seems to be room to share the lane, motorcycles need extra space to turn safely.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you:

options.text: May turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
Cannot turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
Do not have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign warns that:

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: The "Four-second rule" refers to:

options.text: How to yield to other cars.
How to turn at stop signs.
How to follow another car.
How to cross an intersection.

questions.explanation: On dry roads, leave at least four seconds between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their back that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: On a dry highway, a safe following distance is at least:

options.text: Three seconds.
Two seconds.
Four seconds.
Two car lengths.

questions.explanation: On a dry highway, a four-second gap between you and the car ahead gives you enough time to steer or brake to avoid a crash.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Continue through the intersection normally.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop until the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on a wet road, your tires cannot remove water from the surface. At very high speeds, your tires may lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors for tailgaters. If someone is too close, slow down gradually or change lanes to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because a driver is following too closely.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. They are on the sides and behind your car.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well before your exit. Only slow down after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter—only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.
